title: Walking by Faith
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Walking by faith means living by trust in God’s character, promises, Word, and faithfulness rather than by sight, fear, feelings, or earthly certainty. Faith looks to God when His work is not yet fully seen.
summary: Walking by faith means living by trust in God’s character, promises, Word, and faithfulness rather than by sight, fear, feelings, or earthly certainty. Faith looks to God when His work is not yet fully seen.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the object and foundation of saving faith. Believers walk by faith because Christ is faithful, His promises are true, and His resurrection guarantees the hope still unseen.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Christian life is lived by faith. Believers do not always see what God is doing, understand His timing, or feel strong confidence. Yet they are called to trust the God who has spoken and proven Himself faithful in Christ.

Faith is not imagination or denial of reality. Abraham believed God’s promise even when circumstances seemed impossible. Faith takes God at His Word because God is true, powerful, and faithful.

Walking by faith is daily reliance on Christ. The believer lives not by self-confidence, but by faith in the Son of God who loved him and gave Himself for him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people are ruled by what they can see, control, or feel. When circumstances are painful or unclear, faith may seem weak. But Scripture teaches that the righteous live by faith, not by visible certainty.

This doctrine steadies believers in waiting, suffering, decision-making, and obedience. Faith rests on God’s Word when emotions rise and fall.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Trust God in the next step before you can see the whole path. Bring your doubts honestly to Him, remember His promises, and obey what He has made clear. Let faith in Christ govern your choices more than fear, pressure, or circumstances.
